title: Pipeline concurrency playbook: prefetch vs emit (WIP)
content:
Purpose:

- Capture a pragmatic playbook for coordinating prefetch/prefill work with decode/emit work when we want overlap but still meet tight tail-latency SLOs.
- Surface heuristics that can be implemented in the slot allocator + KV residency tracker without touching core kernel code.
- Collect measurable signals, safe defaults, and an experiment plan for greenfield rollout.

Context and assumptions (short):

- Serving runtime supports: prefill (attention/kv warmup), decode (autoregressive emit), streaming responses.
- We assume a single physical slot can house either prefill slices or decode work; some hardware can do partial overlap but simpler model: slot dedicated per-step.
- KV cache is the primary cross-request state; hit rate has large effect on decode latency.
- Workloads: mix of interactive short-turn chats and long-generation background batches; interactive wants P99 < 200ms for token emits.

Problems we want to solve:

1) Avoid interactive decode stalls caused by long prefill runaway tasks.
2) Leverage prefill work opportunistically (prefetch/kv rejuvenation) to reduce overall token cost without sacrificing tail for interactive streams.
3) Prevent priority inversion when many background prefetches flood the slot pool.

Design goals and constraints:

- Deadline-awareness: streams carry soft deadlines for next-token emit (derived from SLA and client expectation).
- Graceful degradation: if prefill can't complete before deadline, do a lightweight decode path that tolerates partial KV.
- Low coupling: most heuristics live in the scheduler/slot allocator and the KV residency tracker; kernels remain stable.
- Telemetry first: every heuristic must be backed by a metric and a fallback path.

High-level approach (playbook):

1) Two-tier stream lanes (fast / background):
   - Fast lane: interactive requests. Strong deadline weighting, preemptible background work allowed to be evicted.
   - Background lane: low-priority prefetch/backfill work, long windows, high batching allowed.
   - Streams start in fast lane by default; background tasks created by separate controllers (cache warmers, bulk ingestion) go to background lane.

2) Deadline-aware microbatch formation (deadline-window batching):
   - Each incoming decode request carries next-decode-deadline T_deadline.
   - Batch microbatches only if waiting time < soft_window (e.g., 10ms) and adding the request does not push estimated batch decode time past T_deadline.
   - If T_deadline is tight, form single-request microbatch (decode-first preference).

3) Prefetch slices (opportunistic KV warms):
   - Prefetch slices are small prefill tasks targeted at high-likelihood KV entries for imminent decodes (based on prefix n-gram reuse / embeddings).
   - Size-limit prefetch slice to X tokens per stream (configurable, default X=8) to bound stall effects.
   - Track prefetch success rate and abort conditions (if decode is scheduled before prefetch completes, prefetch becomes orphaned and may be canceled).

4) Stream leasing and slot eviction policy:
   - When a slot is assigned to background prefill, it holds a short lease (lease_ms). If a fast-lane request needs a slot and none idle, the scheduler can evict background lease if eviction_budget allows.
   - Eviction budget: per-GPU soft budget to avoid thrashing (e.g., at most 20% of background prefill slots evicted per second).
   - Eviction respects a per-stream anti-starvation credit: streams that have been repeatedly evicted gain a credit making them less evictable.

5) KV residency epochs and pinning heuristics:
   - Each KV region (per key or chunk) is tagged with an epoch counter and a resident_score (float).
   - When prefill touches KV entries for an active stream, increase resident_score by hit_gain; resident_score decays over time (exponential decay).
   - Pinning: if resident_score > pin_threshold for a high-SLA stream, the scheduler will prefer slots/placement that keep that KV chunk resident on the same device for next N tokens.
   - Eviction policy uses deadline-weighted LRU: score = resident_score * expected_future_deadline_weight. Lower score evicted first.

6) Graceful partial-decode path (decode on partial KV):
   - If prefill not finished by T_deadline, decode kernel can operate with partial KV (fallback kernels with slightly higher compute but avoid full stall).
   - Use confidence-based rerank: if partial KV yields low-confidence token (below threshold), scheduler can trigger immediate background re-prefetch and mark emit as tentative or insert a short follow-up correction.

7) Prefill vs decode handoff markers (protocol):
   - Introduce a lightweight handoff token: {stream_id, prefill_epoch, handoff_barrier_id}.
   - Prefill posts barrier when it completed necessary slices. Decode will check barrier; if mismatch, decide fast path (partial decode) or wait (only if slack allows).

Slot allocator sketch (in words):

- Input: incoming work items (type: prefill_slice | decode_request), stream metadata (deadline, lane, resident_score), current slot inventory (idle_slots, prefill_slots, decode_slots).
- Step 1: satisfy fast-lane decode requests preferentially using idle_slots or preemptible prefill_slots within eviction budget.
- Step 2: form deadline-aware microbatches for waiting decodes up to microbatch_limit or until T_deadline risk crosses threshold.
- Step 3: schedule prefetch slices only if global prefetch_cap not exceeded and they won't cause immediate deadline violations for queued decodes on that device.

Priority inversion mitigation (practical heuristics):

- If a background prefill has been running > long_prefill_ms and there are >N fast-lane preemptions targeting the same device, throttle new background starts for a cooldown period.
- Maintain per-device rolling metric: fraction_of_time_serving_fast = sliding window; use as multiplier to reduce background prefetch start rate.
- Anti-hammering: if eviction_budget exhausted, fast-lane requests fall back to regional routing or compatible smaller models rather than thrash slots.

Metrics / telemetry (must ship first):

- Per-device: prefill_slot_utilization, decode_slot_utilization, eviction_rate, eviction_latency_impact (P50/P95 increase after eviction).
- Per-stream: kv_hit_rate_predecode, prefill_completion_before_deadline_pct, decode_partial_path_pct, emit_p99_latency, token_cost.
- Global fairness: Gini-index over per-stream latency delta vs baseline.

Experiment plan (phased rollout):

- Phase A: internal canary (1 device pool). Enable deadline-aware batching only; measure P95/P99 delta.
- Phase B: add short prefetch slices + stream leasing; tune eviction_budget to keep tail stable.
- Phase C: enable pinning for top-10% high-SLA customers and run for 2 weeks.
- Phase D: widen to background warmers + telemetry-based dynamic prefetch_cap.

Open questions / TODOs:

- What is the right default soft_window for batching across model families? (Small models tolerate larger microbatches.)
- How big should prefetch_slice be for long-context models (LLAMA-2 style) vs short ones?
- We need a cost-safety circuit: do not let prefetch doubling increase unit-cost beyond X% per minute.
- Implementation TODOs: add handoff_barrier metadata to RPC proto; expose resident_score in debug traces; implement eviction_budget circuit.

Notes to self / action items:

- [ ] Prototype lease eviction hook in slot allocator (Ravi)
- [ ] Add resident_score decay and pin_threshold config (Priya)
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards: eviction_impact, partial_decode_rate (Evan)
- [ ] Wire up linked GHPR SRV-812 for microbatch estimator changes

References and other reading:

- Past experiments: see SRV-142 (microbatch latency vs batch size), SRV-273 (KV pinning experiment log).
- Related: kernel-level optimistic decode fallback document (kernel team) — we should coordinate kernel fallback costs with scheduler heuristics.

End of playbook (working draft).

Questions/comments welcome. This is intentionally prescriptive/operational rather than purely theoretical — the goal is to ship a safe default and iterate with telemetry.
